validity.recommendation: No action — existence confirmed independently, keep as a distinct entity.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed by 2 independent sources that name this pipeline specifically and are NOT gem.wiki-derived: (1) cdu.ru (Russia's Central Fuel-Energy Dispatch Directorate, ЦДУ ТЭК), 'Казахстан: транспортировка и транзит газа', July 3 2023 — lists 'Оренбург — Новопсков' by name among the main gas pipelines transiting Kazakhstan, capacity 14.6 bcm/y; (2) eegas.com (East European Gas Analysis, M. Korchemkin), 'Russian-Ukrainian Gas Dispute' Table 1 — lists 'Orenburg-Novopskov' by name as a 1-line Russian gas import pipeline into Ukraine, entry point Sokhranovka GMS, capacity 18 bcm/yr. These are two genuinely separate origins (Russian state dispatch center vs. independent US gas-industry analyst), so tier=high. The gem.wiki-cited qazaqgaz.kz press release (fire at '288 km of MG Orenburg-Novopskov, UMG Uralsk') would have been a third, very specific confirmation but is now dead (HTTP 404, confirmed via url_verifier) — noted for the record, not cited.

validity.recommendation: No merge — P0791 is a distinct physical trunk from the 'Soyuz' (Orenburg-Western Border of USSR) pipeline, despite name/route overlap near Novopskov. No action needed.
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE CHECK (against Soyuz, not on the 39-row roster but a name-confusable neighbor): ru.wikipedia's 'Союз (газопровод)' article gives Soyuz as Orenburg→Uralsk→Aleksandrov Gai→Kremenchug→Dolyna→Uzhhorod, 2,750 km, 1,420 mm, 26 bcm/y, commissioned 1980 — Novopskov is listed only as an intermediate compressor-station town on Soyuz's route to Uzhhorod, not an endpoint. Two independent ru.wikipedia articles (Меловский район; Энергетическая политика Казахстана) both list 'Оренбург — Новопсков' and 'Союз'/'Оренбург — Западная граница' as two SEPARATE named high-pressure pipelines passing through the same corridor — confirming P0791 is its own distinct 1,220 mm / ~14.6 bcm/y trunk terminating at Novopskov, not a mislabeled Soyuz segment. Checked against the 39-pipeline Ukraine-gas roster: no name/spec collision with any other row (P0789 Urengoy-Novopskov and P0790 Petrovsk-Novopskov are separate, differently-sourced trunks that happen to converge at the same Novopskov hub — a real, well-documented multi-trunk junction, not duplication).

Оренбург — Новопсков'), i.e. a transmission trunk, not a gathering/process/feeder line. Fuel=Gas is unambiguous throughout. No classification concern.

Do not add Gazprom as owner of the Ukrainian section.
validity.researcher_notes: OWNER: current sheet has Owner1=Gazprom PJSC, Owner2=QazaqGaz, no percentages, and no Ukrainian entity at all. Per the country-wide rule, Gazprom does not own any Ukrainian section, and on a genuinely cross-border row the correct reading is a split by country. This row is unusual among the 39-pipeline roster in that it is Russia+Kazakhstan(transit)+Ukraine, not just Russia+Ukraine — cdu.ru's article, about Kazakhstan's gas transportation and transit, groups Orenburg-Novopskov among the pipelines transiting Kazakhstan, so Gazprom (Russia section) + QazaqGaz's Intergas Central Asia subsidiary (Kazakhstan/Uralsk transit section) is directionally plausible. But: (1) I could not find a currently-live source naming QazaqGaz specifically as an owner/operator of THIS pipeline — the direct gem.wiki-cited evidence (qazaqgaz.kz press release) 404s; kase.kz only confirms QazaqGaz (KZTG) exists as an entity, not its link to this line, so it is circumstantial support at best; and (2) no owner is recorded for the Ukrainian leg at all, which is a real gap, not a deliberate 100%-foreign-owned situation. Recommending Update research a citable current source for both points rather than staging a value change on weak grounds.

validity.recommendation: Add a ResearcherNotes line documenting Kazakhstan transit (the schema's Start/End fields can't record a third, transit-only country); separately, verify Novopskov's current front-line status before touching EndCountryOrArea/Location — do not assert occupied or Ukrainian-controlled without dated current sourcing.
validity.researcher_notes: LOCATION: StartLocation=Orenburg/Russia and EndLocation=Novopskov/Luhansk Oblast/Ukraine are both independently confirmed (eegas.com's import-pipeline table; the two ru.wikipedia district/energy-policy articles). But the pipeline's real route runs Orenburg (Russia) -> through Kazakhstan (Uralsk region — corroborated by cdu.ru's 'transportation and transit of gas' framing and, historically, the qazaqgaz.kz fire notice at km 288 of the line's 'UMG Uralsk' section, though that specific URL is now dead) -> back into Russia -> Novopskov (Ukraine). GEM's schema has no field for a transit-only third country, so this is a documentation gap, not a wrong value — flagging for a ResearcherNotes addition, not a field change. Separately: gem.wiki's own page (read for leads only, never cited) asserts Novopskov is 'considered occupied by Russia and part of the Lugansk People's Republic' — but Novopskov (Starobilsk Raion, Luhansk Oblast) was inside the area contested/retaken during Ukraine's September 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive, and I could not independently verify its CURRENT (2026) control status — the one lead on this (radiosvoboda.org, dated 2022-04-05, i.e. before the counteroffensive) returned HTTP 403 on fetch and its dateline predates any retaking, so it cannot settle the question either way. This is worth a dedicated check in a future pass; I am not proposing any EndCountryOrArea/geography change on this pass.

validity.recommendation: Keep Capacity=14.60 bcm/y for now (it is the more recent, more precise, exact-decimal match), but record the conflicting figure in ResearcherNotes rather than silently passing it — do not treat this as fully resolved.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — Capacity: material disagreement between two independent sources that both name this pipeline specifically. cdu.ru (Russian federal dispatch center, dated July 3 2023) states capacity = 14.6 bcm/year — an EXACT match to GEM's 14.60, and recent enough to plausibly be (or trace to) GEM's actual source. eegas.com (East European Gas Analysis, Jan. 2009 vintage — one of the gem.wiki-cited leads, verified independently live) states capacity = 18 bcm/yr in its Table 1 of Russian import pipelines into Ukraine. That is a ~23% disagreement, which is material per the corroboration standard. Two plausible explanations, neither confirmable from what I could access: eegas's older figure may reflect a different (design/nameplate vs. technical-through-Ukraine) capacity concept, or a since-derated line. Given cdu.ru's recency and exact-decimal match I lean toward confirming GEM's current value, but this should not be read as a clean two-source high-tier confirmation — it is one strong recent match against one older conflicting figure.

validity.recommendation: Leave Length (1230.00 km) and Diameter (1220 mm) as-is but unresolved for refs — chase a Kazakh technical/engineering source (e.g. the Intergas Central Asia network register, or a Soviet-era engineering text) or ENTSOG-adjacent material for the Russia/Kazakhstan portion in a future pass; do not fabricate a citation for these two numbers.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — Length/Diameter: I could not find any independently-verifiable source (gem.wiki-cited or otherwise) that states a numeric length or diameter for this pipeline. cdu.ru explicitly does not give either figure; the Kazakhstan energy-policy and Melovsky-district ru.wikipedia articles mention the pipeline by name but give no technical specs; the gem.wiki-cited qazaqgaz.kz press release that likely had a diameter/route detail (it names a specific km-marker, '288 km', within the Uralsk section) is dead (404). energybase.ru (also gem.wiki-cited) returns a Cloudflare-style access-block interstitial, not the real page — kept as a potential future lead per the never-delete-over-an-access-failure rule, not treated as confirming or refuting anything. So 1,230 km / 1,220 mm are plausible (1,220 mm matches sister pipeline P0790 Petrovsk-Novopskov exactly, consistent with a shared-era, shared-corridor build) but not independently corroborated on this pass.

validity.recommendation: Keep Status=operating per the country-wide rule (physical asset in service); add a ResearcherNotes line noting the Ukraine-bound transit leg specifically has been idle since Sokhranivka's closure.
validity.researcher_notes: STATUS: keeping Status=operating is correct under the country's standing guidance — Status describes the physical asset, and cdu.ru (July 2023) still discusses this pipeline as part of the current Russia/Kazakhstan gas transportation and transit network. However, this line's specific Ukraine entry point is Sokhranovka GMS (per eegas.com's table), and the country note records Sokhranivka's closure by Ukraine on 11 May 2022 as the point at which that specific import route stopped carrying transit gas — gem.wiki's own text (read for leads only) similarly describes the pipeline as now used mainly to supply Orenburg Oblast and southwestern Russia/Kazakhstan consumers, i.e. the Ukraine-bound function is dormant even though the asset overall is in service. This is dated, line-specific evidence (not a generic 'transit stopped' argument), so it belongs in ResearcherNotes as a caveat — but it does not, by itself, justify changing Status away from operating for the whole multi-country row.

fills.researcher_notes: cdu.ru (July 2023) discusses this pipeline as a current, in-service part of Russia/Kazakhstan gas transit — supports operating for the asset as a whole. See validity note on the dormant Ukraine-bound leg (Sokhranivka closure) for the caveat.

cdu.ru (2023) states 14.6 bcm/year, an exact match. See validity concern: eegas.com (2009) states 18 bcm/yr for the same pipeline — a material, unresolved disagreement, so this is staged as a match but flagged, not a clean confirmation.
No independent source found with a numeric length for this pipeline; the one gem.wiki-cited lead most likely to carry it (qazaqgaz.kz press release naming a specific km-marker) is dead (404).

Article states the pipeline runs 'от Оренбургского обогатительного комбината' (from the Orenburg gas-processing plant), confirming the Orenburg field/complex as the fuel source.

eegas.com's import-pipeline table confirms an Orenburg->Ukraine route entering via Sokhranovka GMS; the Melovsky-district article confirms the corridor runs through the Russia/Ukraine border area toward Luhansk Oblast. Caveat (see validity): the real route also transits Kazakhstan (Uralsk), which the schema has no field to record — recommend a ResearcherNotes line, not a field change. Novopskov's current front-line/control status could not be independently confirmed on this pass; do not change EndCountryOrArea without dated current sourcing.

Could not find a currently-live, pipeline-specific citation for either owner. cdu.ru gives circumstantial support for a Kazakhstan-transit role (consistent with QazaqGaz/Intergas Central Asia operating the Uralsk section) but does not name QazaqGaz or this pipeline's ownership directly; kase.kz only confirms QazaqGaz's corporate existence. The gem.wiki-cited source that named this pipeline and KazTransGaz/QazaqGaz together (a fire-notice press release) is dead (404). Separately flagged in validity: no owner at all is recorded for the Ukrainian section, which per the country-wide rule should be the Ukrainian state gas TSO, never Gazprom — recommend Update research this rather than staging an unsupported addition here.

summary: P0791 (Orenburg-Novopskov): existence confirmed independently (cdu.ru + eegas.com, tier=high) and confirmed distinct from the similarly-routed 'Soyuz' pipeline (not a duplicate); classification (gas/transmission) holds. Concerns: Capacity has a material 14.6 vs 18 bcm/y disagreement between a recent exact-match source and an older conflicting one; Length/Diameter have no independent numeric corroboration at all; Owner is missing a Ukrainian-section entity and its QazaqGaz citation is now dead; Location doesn't capture the pipeline's Kazakhstan transit and Novopskov's current occupation/control status is unverified. Status=operating kept per country rule, with the Ukraine-bound leg's 2022 dormancy noted as a caveat.
